name: Battle of Nancy
summary: Charles the Bold, Duke of Burgundy, is killed at the Battle of Nancy on January 5, 1477, fighting a coalition of Swiss Confederation forces and the army of René II of Lorraine. Charles's body is found three days after the battle, face-down in a frozen pond, disfigured by wolves. His death ends the Valois Burgundian state at its apparent zenith. His daughter Mary of Burgundy inherits the vast Burgundian territories; her marriage to Maximilian of Habsburg sets off the conflict that defines early modern European politics.

_quarry.structural_significance: The end of the independent Duchy of Burgundy, the most powerful state between France and the Empire; France reabsorbs the duchy proper; the Burgundian Netherlands pass to the Habsburgs via Mary's marriage, creating the Habsburg inheritance that later becomes the Spanish Netherlands; demonstrates the limits of personal dynastic power without institutional continuity
